ideas.description:
Run one offline screen of a few configs, then launch the best one exactly once. Base is the I119 code: the E081 bundle (E069 + fused per-epoch augment + build-time prepare warmups) plus the paired_gate.py config switch. Run everything in ONE process with one build, seeds 3-32 (30 seeds), configs alternating per seed so they share autotuned kernels, as in I119.

Configs:
- c0 = E081 bundle as is (20 px first stage, 6.75 epochs). Control.
- c1 = I119 cfg1: 18 px first stage, 6.875 epochs, block-1 freeze at 0.8 of total samples (275000).
- c2 = 18 px first stage, 6.9375 epochs (346875 samples). The extra 0.1875 epoch goes into the 32 px stage, the block-1 freeze moves to 277500, and every schedule is indexed by samples seen. The final partial epoch uses the first 0.9375 of its permutation, and the fused augment writes only the consumed samples.
- If the I123 warmup screen promotes an arm, or the outside-step cut (next idea) passes its gate first, add it to c1 and c2. Never add it to c0.

Warm up every new partial shape (277500, the run end) in build() with channels_last tensors (E035), and run debug_nan.py.

Pre-registered launch rule. For each config compute:
- m = 30-seed mean;
- t = offline train+prepare time × (4.506/4.515), the E081 harness/offline calibration;
- P = Φ((m − 0.7530)/0.16), using a 3-seed-mean sd of 0.16 pp from the per-seed sd of ~0.28;
- EV = P × (4.678 − t).
Launch the argmax-EV config once on seeds 0-2 only if P ≥ 0.60 and t ≤ 4.63 s. Do not re-roll. Report seeds 23-32 separately: they are fresh, while seeds 3-22 of c1 already informed I119.
ideas.expected: c1: 30-seed mean 0.7533-0.7542, point ~0.7537 (P ~0.67); time ~4.57 s. c2: mean ~0.7541 (P ~0.75); time ~4.60 s. Most likely c1 or c2 gets launched, with a ~65-75% chance of the first new feasible tip since E069, at 4.57-4.61 s (-1.5% to -2.3% vs 4.678). If neither config meets the rule, the flat frontier (~0.05 pp per 1% of time, for every reallocation) cannot clear the local gate without a real accuracy gain. Then stop launching time-only candidates.

ideas.description:
Cut outside-step work on the E081 bundle while keeping the math (near-)identical. Two changes, both from the I122 trial profile:
(1) Lookahead currently takes 0.039-0.041 s/trial as an eager foreach lerp over params and BN buffers at ~43 syncs. Replace it with ONE torch.compile'd function that takes the param/buffer lists and alpha as a 0-d GPU tensor, warmed up in build() on synthetic tensors of the exact shapes, including the block-1-frozen variant if it differs.
(2) Resizing to 20 px and 28 px currently runs per batch (~0.024 s/trial). Move it into the fused per-epoch augment pass, so each low-res stage resizes its consumed samples once per epoch in the same op order and precision.
Gate offline with synchronized timers over 3 trials (the I122 script). Outside-step time must fall by ≥ 0.025 s/trial. On seeds 3-12 in the same process, paired accuracy against E081 must be within ±1 SE (math unchanged up to lerp rounding). Do not launch alone. If it passes, it becomes the base for the I124-style screen.
ideas.expected: Lookahead falls 0.040 → ~0.015 s and resize ~0.024 → ~0.012 s. Total -0.025 to -0.04 s/trial, i.e. -0.5% to -0.9% (point -0.7%). Accuracy is unchanged in expectation. If the saving is < 0.02 s, close the outside-step axis for good (time is ~98% inside the compiled step).

ideas.description:
Explore Muon momentum on the current base. Proposed new Lvl3 node: H1.2.10, 'Muon momentum is off its optimum at bs 1536 with PE coefficients'. Momentum was set to 0.8 on a single 3-seed run at bs 1024 with plain NS3 (E026, +0.18, inside noise), and was never re-tested after bs 1536, the curriculum, PE or the freeze.
Base: E081 bundle. In ONE process on seeds 3-22, screen two arms against E081 rerun in the same process: Muon Nesterov momentum 0.7 and 0.9. Everything else is unchanged, including lr 0.16, PE NS3, the Frobenius rescale, projection, lookahead and the SGD group. If momentum is a guarded Python constant, each arm recompiles: warm all Muon variants per arm, and ignore the screen's times (as in I120). Promote an arm into the I124 stack only if its paired gain is ≥ +0.12 pp at ≥ 2 SE.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.3%). Paired delta per arm -0.3 to +0.2 pp. Point -0.03 pp for 0.7 and +0.03 pp for 0.9: fewer steps per sample at bs 1536 argue for more averaging before orthogonalization. A gain ≥ +0.12 pp at 2 SE would be a free buffer worth ~2.5% of time. Both arms within 1 SE closes the momentum axis, and with it the last untuned Muon scalar.

ideas.description:
Explore stronger translation at 32 px. I118 showed that removing translate-2 costs -0.28 pp paired, so augmentation diversity is valuable even at 6.75 epochs, and the stronger side has never been tested (airbench96 uses larger translates on longer runs).
Base: E081 bundle. Make one change: translate 2 → 3 in the 32 px stage only, implemented as pad-3 plus random crop inside the fused augment. The 20/28 px stages stay translate-free, and flip and jitter are unchanged. Shapes are unchanged. Re-warm the augment variant in build() and check that the fused augment's RNG draws for all 50k samples are still generated.
Screen in ONE process on seeds 3-22, paired against E081 in the same process. Promote into the stack only if the paired gain is ≥ +0.12 pp at ≥ 2 SE.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.2%). Paired delta -0.25 to +0.25 pp, point +0.03 pp. A gain ≥ +0.12 pp at 2 SE is a free buffer and reopens augmentation strength (translate 4, or cutout, next). A drop ≥ 0.15 pp means translate-2 sits at its optimum, which closes H1.8 in both directions.

ideas.description:
Explore per-block Muon lr. Proposed new Lvl3 node: H1.2.11, 'blocks want different rotation rates'. H7 shows block 1 is nearly done by 0.8 while block 2 is still learning at 0.9 (E062), yet all blocks share lr 0.16. Global lr changes hit cliffs on both sides (0.12: -0.89; 0.20 under PE: -0.17 paired), so a per-block split is the only untested lr shape.
Base: E081 bundle. Two arms in ONE process on seeds 3-22, paired against E081 in the same process:
(a) block-1 shape groups at lr 0.13, blocks 2/3 at 0.16;
(b) block-2 and block-3 groups at 0.19, block 1 at 0.16.
Pass a per-group lr multiplier as 0-d tensors into the batched compiled Muon step (both freeze variants), so arms do not recompile. Promote only if the paired gain is ≥ +0.12 pp at ≥ 2 SE.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged. Paired delta per arm -0.35 to +0.2 pp, point -0.05 pp, since the global cliffs suggest 0.16 is near-optimal for every block. A gain ≥ +0.12 pp would be a free buffer and would localize where the lr cliff comes from. Both arms within 1 SE closes the Muon lr axis in every shape.

ideas.description:
Gate first in drafts/, untimed. On the E081 bundle, profile the batched compiled Muon step with and without the weight-norm projection (cuda events and the profiler, both freeze variants). The step takes ~1.43 ms/step, of which NS GEMMs are ~1.13 ms, so projection plus momentum plus norms are ≤ 0.3 ms. If the projection costs < 0.12 ms/step (< ~0.026 s/trial, ~0.6%), retire H2.4.3 without a run.
If it costs more, make one change: project only on steps where step % k == 0, with k = 2 + int(15 × progress), and always on the final step. Use two compiled Muon variants chosen in Python by step index, all warmed in build(). Screen in ONE process on seeds 3-22 against E081. Promote into the stack only if paired accuracy is ≥ -0.05 pp and offline time is ≤ -0.8%.
ideas.expected: ~70% chance the gate fails (projection is fused and ~0.05-0.1 ms/step), and H2.4.3 is retired. If it passes: time -0.6% to -1.2%. Paired accuracy -0.2 to +0.1 pp, point -0.05 pp, because filter norms drift between projections without the Muon weight decay Hiverge pairs it with.

structured_output.summary:
Where things stand: every reallocation of time now trades at about 0.05 pp per 1% of time. That covers epochs (I114), the freeze points (E079), the 25 px middle stage (I113), the late batch ramp (I110) and width (I105), so none of them helps on net. The averaging, logit-scale, pooling and translate-removal axes are closed, and the residual check (I121) did not apply. Autotune nondeterminism cannot be removed (I117), so every launch is a fresh draw around the recipe's true mean.

The only realistic route to the gate is to spend the math-preserving bundle (E081, -3.7%) on a small epoch buffer.

**Lead idea (I124, priority 5).** A one-process, 30-seed screen of:
- the E081 control;
- I119 cfg1 (18 px first stage, 6.875 epochs);
- a 6.9375-epoch version of cfg1.

It replaces I119's arbitrary mean ≥ 0.7540 bar with a launch rule fixed in advance: estimated pass probability × time saved. Launch once only if pass probability ≥ 0.6 and time ≤ 4.63 s. The expected outcome is a ~70% chance of the first new feasible tip, at ~4.57-4.61 s.

**Supporting exploit ideas.**
- A cut to outside-step work: compile the lookahead blend and resize each low-res stage once per epoch. Expected saving ~0.7%, folded into the stack rather than launched alone.
- A gate-first check of how often the Muon weight-norm projection runs (priority 1). It is likely to retire H2.4.3 without a run.

**Explore screens.** Each needs ≥ +0.12 pp at 2 SE before it is promoted into the stack:
- Muon momentum 0.7 / 0.9, untuned since bs 1024 and the old Newton-Schulz coefficients;
- translate 3 at 32 px, the untested stronger side of augmentation;
- per-block Muon lr.

I123 (warmup screen) is still running, and any arm it promotes gets folded into I124. No queued ideas needed dropping: everything except I123 is already done or dropped.
